newsitem.title: USA: U.S. tentatively backs United/Air Canada pact.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tentatively backs United/Air Canada pact.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Transportation said Friday it was tentatively granting United Airlines and Air Canada antitrust immunity to allow them to establish on operating alliance.

"With the potential integration of these two carriers' transborder services, we continue to reap the benefits of the Clinton administration's open-transborder aviation agreement with Canada," said Transportation Secretary Rodney Slater in a statement.
The approval excluded certain U.S. passengers in the Chicago/San Francisco-Toronto markets and all-cargo and third-country services.
The Department said it would consider responses from interested parties before reaching a final decision.

United, a unit of UAL Corp, and Air Canada, are part of a larger operating pact known as the Star Alliance which also groups Germany's Lufthansa, Scandinavian Airlines Systems, Thai Airways and Brazil's Varig.
As part of the U.S. approval, United and Air Canada will be required to file additional data on Star Alliance.

Although the airlines will keep their separate identities, there will be coordination of routes, joint marketing, and code-sharing flights which allow passengers to be passed easily from one partner to another.

The Department of Transportation said it found that granting approval would enhance competition in the U.S.-Canada market, increase operating efficiency and provide the traveling public with better service.
